newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. official says Kabul may fall to Taleban.
newsitem.headline: U.N. official says Kabul may fall to Taleban.

text.p: A top U.N. official confirmed on Wednesday that the Afghan Taleban militia had reached Kabul and said they could be on the verge of taking the city.
"It is possible that Kabul is going to fall," U.N. Under-Secretary General Marrack Goulding told reporters in New York. Goulding is in in touch with U.N. officials in the Afghan capital.
Goulding, who visited Afghanistan last week, said he hoped the U.N. Security Council would endorse an appeal for a ceasefire and negotiations in the country when it meets later on Wednesday.
But he said there had been signs that government troops were defecting or refusing to fight in the face of the Taleban attacks, both in Kabul and other cities.
"We are getting indications ... that Kabul may be on the point of falling," he said.
"If the Taleban think they achieve their objectives by military means, it's going to be very difficult to persuade them to get into negotiations," Goulding added.
